LESSON: READING ALOUD: PHONETIC AWARENESS PRONUNCIATION PHRASING VOICE PROJECTION

Grade: Grade 4
Subject: FRENCH
Strand: Strand 2
Topic 2.3: Reading aloud: Phonetic awareness Pronunciation Phrasing Voice projection

SECTION 1: WELCOME

Hello! This is a study lesson on Reading aloud: Phonetic awareness Pronunciation Phrasing Voice projection. Read the explanation, follow every worked example, then do the practice. This is original CBC Learn content written from KICD outcomes — not a copy of a commercial textbook.

Big question: Which places is reading aloud done?

SECTION 2: WHAT YOU WILL LEARN

By the end of this lesson, you will be able to:

1. recognize words in context when reading
2. read aloud simple words with accurate pronunciation

SECTION 3: STUDY NOTES (READ AND LEARN)

WHAT YOU ARE STUDYING: READING ALOUD: PHONETIC AWARENESS PRONUNCIATION PHRASING VOICE PROJECTION
Subject: FRENCH · Grade: Grade 4
This is a learner study lesson (not a teacher guide). Read every part, follow the models, then practise.

BIG PICTURE
Reading aloud: Phonetic awareness Pronunciation Phrasing Voice projection helps you succeed in FRENCH. You will understand it, practise it, and use it at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

KEY FACTS: READING ALOUD: PHONETIC AWARENESS PRONUNCIATION PHRASING VOICE PROJECTION
Language skills grow by daily practice: listen carefully, speak clearly, read every day, write neatly.
Model → guided practice → independent practice.
Always use complete sentences when writing answers.

PART 1: Recognize words in context when reading

What this means
In this part you learn to recognize words in context when reading. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: recognize words in context when reading.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model reading: Read a short paragraph about “Reading aloud: Phonetic awareness Pronunciation Phrasing Voice projection”, then retell it in 3 sentences.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can recognize words in context when reading. Write or say your answer clearly.

PART 2: Read aloud simple words with accurate pronunciation

What this means
In this part you learn to read aloud simple words with accurate pronunciation. You will use ideas from at school, at home, and in your community in Kenya.

How to learn it
1. Read the idea carefully: read aloud simple words with accurate pronunciation.
2. Listen, speak, read, then write using a Kenyan example from your life.
3. Check yourself: Can you explain it without looking?

Model
Model speaking: Say 4 clear sentences about Reading aloud: Phonetic awareness Pronunciation Phrasing Voice projection to a partner.

Your turn
Do one short practice that proves you can read aloud simple words with accurate pronunciation. Write or say your answer clearly.

PUT IT TOGETHER
Close your notes and say aloud: what Reading aloud: Phonetic awareness Pronunciation Phrasing Voice projection is, one example, and one way you will practise this week.

SECTION 4: QUICK EXAMPLES

Example 1: Read a short paragraph about “Reading aloud: Phonetic awareness Pronunciation Phrasing Voice projection”, then retell it in 3 sentences. (skill: recognize words in context when reading)

Example 2: Say 4 clear sentences about Reading aloud: Phonetic awareness Pronunciation Phrasing Voice projection to a partner. (skill: read aloud simple words with accurate pronunciation)

SECTION 5: PRACTICE NOW

1. Write 5 sentences (or show 5 clear steps) that teach Reading aloud: Phonetic awareness Pronunciation Phrasing Voice projection to a classmate.
2. Practise this skill: recognize words in context when reading.
3. Practise this skill: read aloud simple words with accurate pronunciation.
4. Make one local Kenya example of Reading aloud: Phonetic awareness Pronunciation Phrasing Voice projection from your county, market, farm, or school.
5. Mark your own work: What did you get right? What will you redo?

SECTION 6: WORK TO DO (HOME / REVISION)

1. In your exercise book, make a one-page revision sheet for Reading aloud: Phonetic awareness Pronunciation Phrasing Voice projection: meaning, 3 examples, 5 practice items.
2. Teach a parent/guardian or younger sibling one part of this lesson (2 minutes).
3. Answer in writing: Why should a Grade 4 learner study Reading aloud: Phonetic awareness Pronunciation Phrasing Voice projection?
4. Prepare for the quiz: cover the Remember box and recite it.

SECTION: THINK ABOUT IT

1. Which places is reading aloud done?

SECTION: REMEMBER

1. Know what Reading aloud: Phonetic awareness Pronunciation Phrasing Voice projection means in your own words.
2. Use local Kenyan examples, not only definitions.
3. Practise in small steps, then check your work.
4. Be able to: recognize words in context when reading.
5. Be able to: read aloud simple words with accurate pronunciation.

Now complete the Revision Quiz. Open Answers only after you finish.

— CBC Learn · Original study notes from KICD outcomes (Strategy 2)
